items.text: Moving, even across a county line in Northern Virginia, can open a Special Enrollment Period. Plan availability is set by county, so a move from Fairfax to Arlington can change what is offered to you. honorbrook-insurance.com

A local detail worth knowing before you move, not after.

Medicare Advantage and Part D plan availability is set county by county. Northern Virginia packs a lot of jurisdictions into a small area, so a move that takes twenty minutes can put you in a different service area with a different set of plans, different networks and different drug pricing. Fairfax County, Arlington County, the City of Alexandria and Falls Church are separate for this purpose even when the drive between them is short.

Two consequences. First, a permanent move out of your plan's service area generally triggers a Special Enrollment Period, so you are not stuck waiting for the annual window. Second, if you move and do nothing, you can end up disenrolled from a plan that no longer serves your address, which is a worse way to find out.

This also applies to adult children moving a parent closer. The plan that worked in one county may not exist in the next one.

If a move is coming, tell us the new address before the boxes are packed.

Serving Vienna, Tysons, McLean, Fairfax, Arlington, Falls Church, Reston, Herndon, Oakton and Alexandria. honorbrook-insurance.com

We do not offer every plan available in your area. Any information we provide is limited to those plans we do offer in your area. Please contact Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE to get information on all of your options.
